title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1 was sustained, particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5; Issues 2 and 3 were denied. The matter was remanded for a focused new hearing on clarification and protective steps concerning identified errors.
first_summary: Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning Revoice 18, its denial of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. The SJC sustained the first issue because Presbytery used an incorrect constitutional standard and inadequately addressed errors it had identified. It denied the other issues and remanded for a new hearing on steps needed to clarify those errors and protect the broader Church’s peace and purity.
summary: Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s approval of six theological judgments concerning teachings at Revoice 18, its rejection of his procedural point of order, and its refusal to debate gay-couple adoption. The SJC sustained only the first issue, particularly as to Judgments 2, 3, and 5: Presbytery improperly imported BCO 34-5’s ministerial-process standard into court review and then inadequately addressed identified errors affecting church peace and purity. It rejected the procedural and adoption claims and remanded for a focused new hearing under BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f).

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption identifies Case 2020-05 and the SJC decision on complaint; the final decision was adopted 22–2–0 (lines 11, 287–291; printed pp. 826, 843).
evidence_notes.dispute: The three issues challenged six theological judgments, denial of a point of order, and refusal to debate gay-couple adoption (lines 117–125; printed p. 832).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Issue 1 was sustained and Issues 2–3 denied; the majority found conflation of BCO 34-5 with BCO 40-5 and inadequate action under BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f), then ordered a focused new hearing (lines 127–141, 175–199, 215–247, 249–283; printed pp. 832–843).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The remand need address particularly Judgments 2, 3, and 5. Interaction with the AIC report was encouraged, but that report lacked constitutional status (lines 281–287; printed p. 843). Separate concurrences and dissents were not treated as the court’s holding.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. The AIC report was merely suggested for consideration and expressly lacked constitutional status (lines 283–285; printed p. 843).

source_limits: The synopsis relies solely on the supplied case text. It distinguishes the adopted majority decision from the panel recommendation and separate opinions.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies all three challenged Presbytery actions.
score_reasons.decision: States the sustained issue, both denied issues, and remand.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the incorrect standard and resulting inadequate response.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between ministerial-process standards and standards governing a church court’s response to erroneous opinions.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the majority holding from committee findings, the panel proposal, and separate opinions.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the dispute, result, and limited remand.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative judgments and amends at lines 127–133 and 281–287. The final summary was tightened to specify that only Issue 1 succeeded, emphasize Judgments 2, 3, and 5, identify the competing BCO standards, and avoid implying that the SJC annulled the six judgments or ordered debate on adoption.
